set_aside.unit: A4: Accepted decision A4 — R4. Authorization guard sequence (policy)
set_aside.subject: PLAT-REG-004 request decoding
set_aside.text: “an import or request carrying its own status or project facts is refused at decoding” does not define “project facts”, while accepted snapshot and project-scoped requests themselves carry project_id and other project-related fields.
set_aside.question: Which exact client-supplied fields count as forbidden Registry context or project facts, and which project fields such as project_id remain valid request data?
options: Refuse only Registry-owned context fields such as status, display name, address and customer_ref; accept project_id.
Refuse status but accept all other declared request fields.
Refuse any client-supplied project-related field, including project_id.
set_aside.default_guess: Refuse only Registry-owned context fields and accept the typed project_id required by the operation.

witness.initial: An active producer has access to an active Registry project.
events: The producer submits a valid SnapshotPublication containing its required project_id but no status, display name, address or customer_ref.
outcomes: The request is accepted because project_id is an identity selector, not client-supplied Registry context.
The request is refused at decoding because project_id is a project fact carried by the import.
witness.observer: The producer and the Registry-call observer see whether decoding refuses the request before any Registry call.

set_aside.unit: A9: Accepted decision A9 — R9. Money policy
set_aside.subject: aggregate completed_work_total with no progress records
set_aside.text: A section without progress has completed_work_value None and “is left out of the sum”, while BudgetView and ProgressView require completed_work_total: Decimal and define it as the sum of non-None section values; State 0 says missing data is explicit and never replaced by zero.
set_aside.question: When every active-budget section lacks a progress record, is completed_work_total the empty sum 0.00 or unavailable, and may work_balance be calculated from it?
options: Return completed_work_total 0.00 and calculate work_balance from zero.
Represent completed_work_total and dependent work_balance as unavailable.
Use 0.00 only when the project has no planned work, but unavailable when planned work exists without progress.
set_aside.default_guess: Keep the declared Decimal field and use the empty sum 0.00, while retaining None on each section.

witness.initial: A project has an active budget with work_planned 1000.00, no SectionProgress records, and payments totaling 200.00.
events: A viewer reads the project overview.
outcomes: The overview reports completed_work_total 0.00 and an unused advance payment of 200.00.
The overview reports completed work and work balance as unavailable because no work progress was recorded.
witness.observer: The viewer sees either a confirmed-looking zero and balance or explicit missing data.

set_aside.unit: A18: Accepted decision A18 — Budget and snapshot invariants
set_aside.subject: INV-027 owning-record write coverage
set_aside.text: The test requires checking “every operation that writes an owning record of a view — inclusion, allocations, progress, payment, plan and budget-version activation among them”, but “among them” leaves the required operation and record set open.
set_aside.question: What is the exhaustive set of owning records and write operations that INV-027's Required test must cover?
options: Only the six named operation families.
Every writer affecting BudgetView and financial aggregates, with an explicit closed list.
Every writer affecting any ProjectOverview component, including document and photo mutations.
set_aside.default_guess: Cover every writer that can change a budget, expense, progress, payment or photo overview component, and enumerate that set in the test.

witness.initial: A project has a visible expense document and an otherwise stable overview.
events: Staff changes the document visibility, writing an owning ExpenseDocument record.
The next project overview is read.
outcomes: Document visibility is in INV-027's write coverage, so the test must prove the next read recomputes it.
INV-027 covers only the named financial writers, so document visibility is outside this test.
witness.observer: The State 8 verifier sees whether the document mutation must be exercised by the budget-derivation check.

set_aside.unit: A22: Accepted decision A22 — Transaction guard policy (accepted Factory spec, 2026-07-25)
set_aside.subject: TXN-002 Required test
set_aside.text: The only descriptive test says the store “rejects a nested begin and requires exactly one close per call”; the added line “TXN-001, TXN-002: the transaction guard check” binds a check but does not say what must demonstrate that a domain error is re-raised unchanged and not masked by a close failure.
set_aside.question: Which failure history must the TXN-002 Required test exercise, including what rollback does and what exact exception must reach the caller?
options: A domain error followed by successful rollback must be re-raised unchanged.
A domain error plus a rollback failure must still expose the original domain error.
Both successful-rollback and failing-rollback cases must preserve the original exception object and traceback.
set_aside.default_guess: Exercise both rollback success and rollback failure and require the original domain exception to reach the caller unchanged.

witness.initial: A guarded write transaction is open, and rollback is instrumented to raise a persistence error.
events: The use case raises a domain validation error.
outcomes: The caller receives the original domain validation error, with the rollback error suppressed or attached without replacement.
The caller receives the rollback persistence error because the generic close-once test never specified this combined failure.
witness.observer: The API error mapper and the focused transaction check see different exception types.

set_aside.unit: A25: Accepted decision A25 — HTTP transport policy (accepted Factory spec, 2026-07-31 to 2026-08-06)
set_aside.subject: TRN-001 through TRN-003 Required tests
set_aside.text: The Required tests name three Factory checks and then only map invariant identifiers to check names; they do not describe the requests, handler observations or log sinks that must show each invariant holds.
set_aside.question: What concrete cases must the bound checks exercise for untrusted hosts, oversized bodies, foreign-origin sign-out, missing viewer cookies and secret redaction?
options: One representative case per invariant is sufficient.
Every refusal clause and every credential-bearing header, cookie and secret-like field must be exercised.
A source/configuration inspection may replace runtime refusal and logging cases.
set_aside.default_guess: Exercise each stated refusal independently and inspect all produced log lines for representative authorization, cookie and secret-like values.

witness.initial: Logging is enabled and a viewer-entry request contains a capability secret in a secret-like JSON field.
events: The request is rejected for an oversized body.
The transport layer emits its rejection log.
outcomes: TRN-003 requires this early-rejection log to be checked and the value must be redacted.
The checks cover only normal handler logs, so the early transport rejection may log the secret while all named checks still pass.
witness.observer: The log reader and the State 8 verifier see whether the secret appears.

set_aside.unit: A28: Accepted decision A28 — Clock policy (accepted Factory spec, 2026-08-09; one clock source, coordinator 2026-11-07)
set_aside.subject: accepted representation of source-supplied datetimes
set_aside.text: Source-supplied times are kept as “the same instant, stored offset-naive UTC”, but “their accepted forms and checks” are carried to States 6–7 without stating whether naive values, non-UTC offsets or ambiguous datetimes are accepted.
set_aside.question: Which input datetime forms are accepted, and how is each accepted form converted to offset-naive UTC without changing its instant?
options: Require timezone-aware UTC inputs and strip the UTC tzinfo for storage.
Accept any timezone-aware input, convert it to UTC, then strip tzinfo.
Also accept offset-naive inputs by interpreting them as UTC.
Accept offset-naive values as already normalized but reject non-UTC aware values.
set_aside.default_guess: Accept timezone-aware datetimes with any explicit offset, convert to UTC and strip tzinfo; reject offset-naive source times.

witness.initial: A valid snapshot publication supplies approved_at as the offset-naive datetime 2026-11-08 12:00:00.
outcomes: The portal accepts the value as UTC and stores 2026-11-08 12:00:00 without tzinfo.
The portal rejects the publication because an offset-naive input does not identify an instant.
witness.observer: The producer sees acceptance or rejection, and later readers see the stored timestamp.

set_aside.unit: A28: Accepted decision A28 — Clock policy (accepted Factory spec, 2026-08-09; one clock source, coordinator 2026-11-07)
set_aside.subject: wall-clock read count and audit-writer exception
set_aside.text: The normative rule requires one wall-clock reading per operation and one further audit-writer reading, but CLK-001 tests timestamp equality and TTL arithmetic, while CLK-002's counting test counts only elapsed-clock reads.
set_aside.question: What Required test proves the exact number of wall-clock reads for each operation and for an appended audit record?
options: Count one wall read per operation and exactly one additional wall read per audit append.
Timestamp equality is sufficient even if the clock was read repeatedly.
Count only operations that write more than one timestamp.
set_aside.default_guess: Use a counting wall clock and require one operation read plus exactly one audit-writer read when an audit is appended.

witness.initial: A counting wall clock returns the same fixed datetime on every call.
events: A staff mutation writes created_at and appends an audit record.
The implementation reads the wall clock twice in the use case and once in the audit writer.
outcomes: All stored timestamps satisfy equality-based CLK-001 tests even though the operation violated the one-read rule.
A counting test fails because the operation took two reads before the audit writer's permitted further read.
witness.observer: Only a counting-clock test sees the difference; persisted records look identical.

set_aside.unit: A28: Accepted decision A28 — Clock policy (accepted Factory spec, 2026-08-09; one clock source, coordinator 2026-11-07)
set_aside.subject: persisted UTC representation verification
set_aside.text: The normative rule says persisted timestamps are offset-naive UTC, but neither CLK-001 nor CLK-002's Required tests require checking portal-owned timestamps for tzinfo removal or UTC normalization.
set_aside.question: Which Required test demonstrates that every persisted portal-owned and accepted source-supplied instant is represented as offset-naive UTC?
options: Inspect representative persisted rows from every timestamp-producing operation.
Enforce the representation in a shared persistence type and test that boundary once plus source conversions.
Rely on equality with the clock value without separately checking representation.
set_aside.default_guess: Enforce and test the shared persistence boundary, with representative tests for portal-owned and source-supplied timestamps.

witness.initial: The wall-clock port returns an aware UTC datetime and the store accepts aware datetimes.
events: A session-creation operation persists created_at and expires_at.
outcomes: The implementation stores aware UTC values; equality and TTL tests pass.
The implementation strips tzinfo and stores offset-naive UTC values as the normative rule requires.
witness.observer: A database reader or representation-focused test sees tzinfo present in one outcome and absent in the other.

set_aside.unit: A28: Accepted decision A28 — Clock policy (accepted Factory spec, 2026-08-09; one clock source, coordinator 2026-11-07)
set_aside.subject: CLK-002 witness binding
set_aside.text: CLK-002 has a Required tests item, but no Required tests line carrying a [witness: ...] tag binds CLK-002 to an existing check; the only witness lines bind CLK-001.
set_aside.question: Which existing witness check asserts CLK-002's source exclusivity, elapsed-read count, boundary decision and non-persistence requirements?
options: Bind CLK-002 to an existing focused verification check.
Add a distinct clock-source verification check and bind it.
Treat the untagged source/counting test prose as sufficient without a witness binding.
set_aside.default_guess: Add or identify a dedicated clock-source verification check and bind CLK-002 to it.

witness.initial: State 2 is handed to witness resolution with the two existing CLK-001 bindings only.
events: It attempts to find the check responsible for CLK-002.
outcomes: CLK-002 is treated as unbound and the handoff fails.
A later author silently assigns CLK-002 to one of the CLK-001 checks despite no binding in the text.
witness.observer: The decision-witness resolver sees the missing or silently invented binding.

set_aside.unit: A28: Accepted decision A28 — Clock policy (accepted Factory spec, 2026-08-09; one clock source, coordinator 2026-11-07)
set_aside.subject: elapsed-clock read on rejected viewer-entry requests
set_aside.text: The clock policy requires “one reading per viewer-entry request”, while A25 refuses untrusted-host and oversized requests before a handler and says the elapsed clock measures the viewer-entry rate-limit window only; the texts do not say whether transport refusals that occur before rate limiting consume the reading.
set_aside.question: Does every request targeting viewer entry take one elapsed reading, or only a request that reaches the rate-limit stage after earlier transport checks pass?
options: Read elapsed time for every request whose route is viewer entry, even if host or body validation refuses it.
Read elapsed time only after trusted-host and body-size checks admit the request to the rate-limit stage.
The transport-check ordering may vary as long as no session is created.
set_aside.default_guess: Take the elapsed reading only when the request reaches the rate-limit stage after earlier transport checks.

witness.initial: The counting clock is at zero reads and the viewer-entry route exists.
events: A client sends a viewer-entry request with an untrusted Host header.
outcomes: The request is refused and the elapsed clock remains unread because trusted-host validation won first.
The request is refused but the elapsed clock records one read because every viewer-entry request must take exactly one.
witness.observer: The counting clock and transport-guard verification see the difference.

set_aside.unit: A32: Accepted decision A32 — Dependency pins and their vulnerability check (owner 2026-11-06: current service behaviour accepted; technical decisions delegated)
set_aside.subject: DEP-002 withdrawn OSV entries
set_aside.text: The normative rule defines a known vulnerability using “an OSV entry that is not withdrawn”, while the Required test says “a listed version ... does not start it” without preserving the non-withdrawn exception.
set_aside.question: Must an installed version listed only by a withdrawn OSV entry block deployment?
options: No; withdrawn entries are ignored as the normative definition states.
Yes; any listed version blocks as the Required test literally states.
A withdrawn entry blocks only when another non-withdrawn entry also marks the version affected.
set_aside.default_guess: Do not block on an entry whose OSV withdrawn field is set, unless another non-withdrawn entry affects the version.

witness.initial: A built image contains distribution D version 1.0, and OSV returns exactly one affected entry for D 1.0 with its withdrawn field set.
events: The deploy gate reads that OSV response in the deploy and evaluates the image.
outcomes: The service starts because no non-withdrawn OSV entry lists the installed version as affected.
The service does not start because the Required test treats any listed version as blocking.
witness.observer: The deploy operator sees whether the same image starts.
